svg.title: Population totals and density in three imaginary areas
svg.desc: Area A has twelve thousand people over two hundred square kilometres, density sixty. B has nine thousand over fifty, density one hundred eighty. C has twenty thousand over four hundred, density fifty. The schematic shaded areas show why total population and density differ.

g.text: One table, two questions: total or density?
Imaginary areas; schematic shapes, not a measured map.
Area People Area km² Shops Shops/1,000
C has most people; B has the highest density. Source: original teaching data.
